fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, class of 2029, and most of my work has been building machine learning and software systems that have to hold up against real users. Right now I work with Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus on the machine learning core of an anomaly detection and alert prioritization system, where I own the event ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so analysts can act on what the model flags. Before that I worked with Intelehealth on AI and data systems for rural telemedicine, including a resource availability scoring pipeline across 32 villages and an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case standard. I also co-founded Open Health Intelligence, where I built ClarityAtlas, an iOS health app in Swift and SwiftUI with passive sleep estimation from HealthKit and Core Motion signals, and shipped it into a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users. Earlier, I served as lead model developer on a Gates Foundation-funded health equity project, training XGBoost models on roughly 10 million survey records.
